dossiers.label: The Seventh Letter: the spark and the five
dossiers.greek: οἷον ἀπὸ πυρὸς πηδήσαντος ἐξαφθὲν φῶς
dossiers.about: There is not and never will be a treatise of Plato's on these things; they cannot be put into words like other studies, but after long living together with the matter, suddenly, like light kindled from a leaping spark, it is born in the soul. For each thing there are name, definition, image and knowledge, and fifth the thing itself; and no one with sense will commit his thoughts to the fixity of writing.

passage.start_quote: οὔκουν ἐμόν γε περὶ αὐτῶν ἔστιν σύγγραμμα οὐδὲ μήποτε γένηται
passage.end_quote: τούτῳ δὴ τῷ μύθῳ τε καὶ πλάνῳ

parts.label: No treatise of mine exists or ever will
parts.quote: οὔκουν ἐμόν γε περὶ αὐτῶν ἔστιν σύγγραμμα οὐδὲ μήποτε γένηται

parts.label: Not sayable like other studies
parts.quote: ῥητὸν γὰρ οὐδαμῶς ἐστιν ὡς ἄλλα μαθήματα

parts.label: Suddenly, like light from a leaping spark
Name, definition, image, knowledge
parts.quote: ἓν μὲν ὄνομα, δεύτερον δὲ λόγος, τὸ δὲ τρίτον εἴδωλον, τέταρτον δὲ ἐπιστήμη

parts.label: No one with sense will set it in writing
parts.quote: νοῦν ἔχων οὐδεὶς τολμήσει ποτὲ εἰς αὐτὸ τιθέναι τὰ νενοημένα ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ

diagram.title: The five of 342a–b, with the circle
diagram.about: The four means of knowing and the fifth, the thing itself, with the letter's own example, the circle.

steps.label: 1. name: 'circle'
steps.quote: κύκλος ἐστίν τι λεγόμενον, ᾧ τοῦτʼ αὐτό ἐστιν ὄνομα

steps.label: 2. definition: equally distant from the centre
steps.quote: τὸ γὰρ ἐκ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἐπὶ τὸ μέσον ἴσον ἀπέχον πάντῃ

steps.label: 3. image: the drawn or turned circle
steps.quote: κύκλος ἕκαστος τῶν ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι γραφομένων ἢ καὶ τορνευθέντων

steps.label: 5. the thing itself, knowable and truly being
steps.quote: ὃ δὴ γνωστόν τε καὶ ἀληθῶς ἐστιν ὄν

echoes.why: The Symposium: suddenly he will see beauty itself.

related.why: The sudden vision at the end of long practice.

web.title: Seventh Letter
web.quote: It also contains an extended philosophical interlude concerning the possibility of writing true philosophical works
